tools.name: purchase-requisition_create
tools.description: Create a reusable purchase-requisition and return its CL-NNNN id: a name, a category and an optional description. Add steps with purchase-requisition_item_add. Free tier: 3 of them, runs unlimited.

tools.name: purchase-requisition_item_add
tools.description: Add one step to a purchase-requisition and return its I01-style id: text, an optional section heading, and required flag. A required step left unanswered or failed blocks sign-off; an optional one does not.

tools.name: purchase-requisition_item_remove
tools.description: Remove one step from a purchase-requisition by its I01-style id and bump the purchase-requisition version. Runs already under way keep the step they started with, so nothing anybody already ticked is rewritten.

tools.name: purchase-requisition_show
tools.description: One purchase-requisition with its steps in order, grouped by section, plus how many are required and how many runs have been started from it. Pass as_text for a blank printable copy with a box against each step.

tools.name: purchase-requisition_list
tools.description: Every purchase-requisition with its category, version, step count and how many runs came from it. Filter by category or by a word in the name. Returns at most 500 rows, newest change first.

tools.name: purchase-requisition_delete
tools.description: Delete a purchase-requisition and its steps for good. Runs already started keep their own copy of the steps and stay readable: deleting the purchase-requisition erases nothing anybody signed.

tools.name: run_start
tools.description: Start a dated run of a purchase-requisition and return its RUN-YYYY-NNNN id. Steps are COPIED into the run, so editing the purchase-requisition later never changes a run under way. Runs are free, never capped.

tools.name: run_check
tools.description: Mark one step pass, fail or na, with who did it and when. na means the step did not apply; it counts as answered and never as passed. A step can be answered again while the run is open, and the last answer stands.

tools.name: run_show
tools.description: The whole run: every step with its answer, who answered it and when, grouped by section, plus the pass, fail and outstanding counts, the failures in full, and whether it can be signed off and why not.

tools.name: run_list
tools.description: Runs newest first, with their purchaseRequisition, progress and sign-off state. Filter by purchaseRequisition, by status, by reference or to open runs only. Returns at most 500 rows.

tools.name: run_sign_off
tools.description: Sign off a completed run with a name and a date, which freezes it. Refused while a required step is unanswered or failed, unless force is true, and either way the exceptions stay on the record and print on the report.

tools.name: run_status
tools.description: Move a run back to open so a step can be answered again, or abandon it when the job did not happen. A signed-off run is refused: a signature is the point at which a run stops moving.

tools.name: run_report
tools.description: The run as plain text on every tier: every step with its mark, who answered it, the notes, the counts and a signature block or the recorded signature. Pro also writes it to out_path as a .txt file.

tools.name: run_delete
tools.description: Delete a run for good, with every answer on it. A signed-off run is refused: it is the record of what somebody put their name to. Abandon a run you no longer want instead of deleting a signed one.

tools.name: license_status
tools.description: Report this endpoint's licence state for your token as JSON: the product, the tier free or pro, why it is not Pro, and the checkout URL. Call it to explain a free-tier refusal. No arguments, nothing changes.

tools.name: license_activate
tools.description: Turn Pro on for this connection with key, an MCPL1.<payload>.<signature> issued at checkout for this server or the bundle. Data under your token stays; a wrong or expired key changes nothing. license_status confirms it.
